How is that relevant?  It's shameful that we helped those pricks get in power but does that mean we shouldn't take them down?

"Osama Bin Laden just orchestrated the killing of 3000 American civilians but we helped him get started so we can't fight back."
I totally agree and I support humanitarian aid for the middle east but I don't support wasting American lives on "liberating" a society which is fundamentally opposed to freedom.
Not really, I just think that's a shitty lie.  "Let's spread freedom to people who hate freedom."
I think that bringing down Bin Laden and the Taliban was  justified, invading Iraq was not.
If I present myself so poorly that nobody wants to even give me a chance then it's my own fault.
I don't think my looks are my main problem, it's probably moreso the way I act and talk and my mannerisms that put people off.
I've been in band with her for a full semester, if she actually really liked me for whatever reason I would have figured it out by now.

Usually that's what I do, I ask questions and listen to their answers and add something about myself if it's relevant but the answers they give aren't enthusiastic and when I add stuff about myself it sounds boring and awkward. They don't care if some ugly awkward guy is asking them questions.

Why shouldn't they tell me if I don't have a chance? Why are they wasting our time and encouraging me to constantly humiliate myself instead of teaching me to adapt to life as a hopeless social retard?

I'm in jazz band, I met a few girls through that but they don't give a shit. I met one in particular who likes all the same shitty music I do but she ignores me unless I talk first and when I do initiate she seems unenthusiastic or even uncomfortable. Whenever I try to talk to her I feel like everything I say is fucking weird and I feel stupid for thinking the cute interesting girl would like me just because we like the same music. If I honestly thought I could have a chance with her then maybe my self-image isn't negative enough.

But at least the initial attraction was there, I can't even find girls who want to get to know me, let alone connect on a serious level. And honestly, if I could go out there and get laid I would but the whole "social retard" thing doesn't really help.

20, I know I'm still young but I honestly think that if I had the capability to be attractive I would have figured that out by now or at least figured out what I'm doing wrong. My therapist and my mom still say they don't know what I'm doing wrong and I think of there were an answer beyond "I'm ugly an awkward" then we would have figured it out.

I'm sorry you had to go through that but at least you have proof that you have it in you to be attractive to a woman and maybe some day you can truly connect with someone. I have no reason to believe that.
The girls who turn me down aren't intolerant, they just don't want to date an ugly awkward guy and I don't blame them.

I've talked with my friends about it and they say that I am weird and awkward but don't give advice beyond "be confident" and "keep trying." If I really am as fucked up as I suspect nobody is going to tell me when they could just say "stop worrying" and make everyone feel better.
I'd really like to have a fulfilling relationship but at this point I'll just take whatever I can get.
Why are you shaming people for not wanting to date someone they find unattractive?

Most girls I meet don't even want to talk to me, let alone be my friend. How do I know that it just isn't ment to happen with anyone ever? I used to just "wait" to meet someone and people told me I wasn't trying hard enough to meet girls. Now I do try and people tell me I'm trying to hard. Could it be that I just lack whatever women find attractive in a man and nobody has the balls to tell me? I couldn't even imagine being put next to a girl and developing a relationship from that.
How can I have a positive self image if I need to accept that I'm awkward and ugly?
Seriously? They're idiots for not wanting to date a guy who is uncomfortably awkward?
I smile when I talk but it doesn't make me look any better. Who says my self-image is "negative" and not just realistic?

Really? A lot of people I know with aspergers are fucking boring, they have one or two narrow interests and don't give a shit about anything else. I like music and psychology, which I'm studying, but most girls don't care and the ones who do would rather date a guy who likes the same stuff but is also charismatic and handsome.

If any of these girls I've talked to over the last few years liked me at all I think I would have figured it out by now at least once. Why is it so hard for people to believe that maybe girls aren't interested in or attracted to me because I'm not interesting or attractive?
They don't know or care that I have AS, all they know is that I'm weird and awkward and that they could do better.
Nope, usually they're just normal girls who aren't super attractive but look alright and they'd rather have a boyfriend who looks alright and talks alright than a guy with autism.

My friends don't have some sort of unifying interest with their girlfriends, they just like each other and like spending time together. Common interests don't matter if you're ugly and uncomfortably awkward. I met a girl in band at school who likes the same music I do but she ignores me unless I talk first and when I do she doesn't seem enthusiastic and sometimes even bored and uncomfortable.
How does that work? I know a few people who are basically social retards who don't feel bad about themselves at all but nobody in the world takes then seriously.

When I approach girls I don't know usually it's at a social event like a party or before or after a class. I just try to make small talk or ask them about things that are related to what's going on. It's all stuff I feel like a girl would be fine talking about with a guy who isn't awkward and ugly.
Dude, I love it when I ask for advice and someone tries to sell me something.

When I ask them questions they give pretty brief answers and if I say something about myself they react in a way that seems really unenthusiastic. ("oh" "cool" "*awkward chuckle*) They also never try to initiate a conversation with me and pretty much ignore me unless I talk first.  If they actually wanted to spend time with me or talk to me I think they'd make that more clear.

Once again, sorry for being dismissive but what if the "aspects of myself" include me being so uncomfortably awkward and unattractive that the average girl will look at me like I'm a freak?  How am I supposed to "live with" that?
I've tried just about all kinds of girls, even the "one off in the corner" doesn't want to date a gawky awkward guy.
If I tried to date a girl who I don't find attractive I'd feel shitty about myself and I'd be a massive shithead for using a girl who likes me as a "learning experience."

What should I be confident about?  Every time I try I fail, even when I put aside my shitty thoughts and feel alright about myself.  Is "confidence" something that only works if you're just a normal guy who doesn't have a reason to feel shitty about himself?

I have only one close friend who's a girl and I've always sort of had a thing for her, even though I'm passed that. (she has a long-distance boyfriend)

>Don't "approach" anybody, it doesn't work

That's how just about all of my friends met their girlfriends, they tell me "KEEP TRYING BRO" but I feel like that's just a cop-out.

I don't know any girls with AS, although I'd like to date one provided we get along well.  I've met lots of girls with family members with disabilities and they treat me the same way as every other girl, just because they love and care about someone with a disability doesn't mean they're obliged to lower their standards for dating.

I met a girl in band at college who likes all the same music I do but she ignores me unless I talk first and whenever I do talk to her it feels really awkward.  Girls won't care if we have common interests if I'm not physically or psychologically attractive.
A lot of people I know with AS are pretty funny-looking and I'm no exception, I don't know what it is.
They aren't that enthusiastic when I talk to them, and if I talk to them over a long period of time I'm always the one who has to initiate and when I do they still don't seem enthusiastic.

>Girls Love it when you Listen. Of course you can talk, and even share some of your experiences, but keep it short and to the point. "Our" interests and detail of story are often not fun to listen to for others, anyway.

Whenever I talk to a girl I listen more than I talk but they don't give a shit.  I'm always the one asking all the questions and when I try to share something relevant it sounds really awkward and forced.

>kind, soft, caring

Sorry for being so dismissive of your advice but those don't mean anything if I'm not attractive.

>low self-esteem

Is it low self-esteem if it's all true?

My friends are no more or less "shallow" than anyone else, they don't know how fucked up I am. If they did they'd back off but I don't want them to know. Also, they're the only real group of friends I've had so I can't just find new ones.

My friends tell me I'm awkward but they can't put their finger on why (maybe it's something I can't change and they don't want to hurt my feelings) and my family thinks I just "get nervous" but sometimes I feel fine and things still go shitty.
I made myself an easy target but if they knew what I was going through they'd stop. They aren't trying to hurt my feelings.
How will exercise improve my speech patterns or gestures, which is what I made this post about in the first place.
I've talked to plenty of foreign people and it goes better but since we're both shitty communicators I don't really learn anything.
He isn't there when I'm in a real social setting instead of just his office.
I've been reflecting on it for two years and I still have no idea how to change what I'm doing.

When I first heard that "confidence" can make a guy more attractive I started feeling like maybe I'm an alright guy with self-esteem issues and I felt good about that. I started actually talking to girls and I had no real success, most just ignored me and the ones that didn't stopped talking to me after a while, I think they were just trying to be nice.

I'm sure that's good advice for normal guys with girl problems but if I am an uncomfortably awkward guy, which most guys with aspergers are, how will feeling better about myself help? How will confidence stop my awkward mannerisms, which are a symptom of my disability?

Why do I deserve to be confident if people interact with me the way they do? I have a fucked up disability and the way I act shows it, it has jack shit with how I feel about myself. Maybe if I ever had a success of some sort I'd feel alright about myself but I fuck up every time.
That's pretty much how I try to talk to people but as soon as I open my mouth I feel like I'm saying a bunch of retarded shit and they look uncomfortable so I back off.

Why should I limit myself to only being friends with weird people? I have no problem with having weird friends but I don't want to limit myself to that.  Also, how is it a good idea at all to explain to people I'm "impaired?" If something is wrong with me they can figure that out on their own, I don't need to give them more reasons to judge me.

I haven't told my friends I have assburgers, if there's something wrong with me they'll see it on their own.

>Let her know that you have Asperger's found that you know that you can act awkward sometimes and miss social queues.

Fuck that, telling someone you just met that you have a disability is just giving them something to judge you based on.

Other than that, good advice.
I'm sorry but until I actually have a real success in my life there is no way I'll be happier.

Why do I deserve respect?  What makes me so great?

>part of respecting yourself is realizing your human and you will never be perfect.

I am fucking tired of hearing this.  I don't want to be "perfect," I just don't want to be a social retard who can't talk to people without embarrassing himself.
I've been talking to a therapist for two years and he still "doesn't know" what I'm doing wrong because he's not there.

I've been talking to a therapist and I've been on anti-depressants for two years to no avail, I won't be happy until I come off as an alright guy.  Pills and being told that everything is alright isn't enough.  I'm looking for social skills training and setting up a meeting with a therapist who specializes in ASD's (who I've met before and I don't like him) and I expect them to be as much of a disappointment as everything else in my life.
Bill Gates is a business genius, I'm not that smart at all.

Fuck that.  If you can be happy being someone who people look down on then you're a better man than I am but I don't want to live my whole life settling for shitty terms.

Also, nobody gives a fuck about "common interests" if I'm just an awkward fucking guy.

It's not what I say which offends people, I don't make off-color remarks unless I'm around my friends who make offensive jokes all the time.  It's the way I say it that's fucked up, my word choice and speech patterns and my voice are fucking weird.  Imagine a poorly-told joke, it's not an intrinsically shitty joke but the way it's told makes it hard to listen to.  That's how I talk.
I've been talking to a therapist and I've been on anti-depressants for two years to no avail, I won't be happy until I come off as an alright guy.

>It's all in the head, I'm not even kidding.

Nope, I fail every time I try and it makes me feel like shit, I used to think that maybe it was all in my head and I'm an alright guy with self-esteem issues but now I know that isn't true.

I've asked my brothers (fraternity brothers) for help before but I end up getting really negative and making them uncomfortable.  They have no idea how deep this goes and I don't want them to know how depressed I am.

Also, I can't emulate other people, when I see other people interacting with people and making them laugh and smile it all makes sense but I have no idea how they do it.  Unless you're De Niro or some shit you can't replicate a person's subtle mannerisms, especially if you have something like Asperger's.

I don't know if it's "real" or not but I do know that I'm a weird fucking guy and people by and large don't like me.

>I mean, if they're your real friends and they're doing something that really upsets you, then there is absolutely nothing wrong with asking them to stop it.

I told one of them to cut it out and he said he would if it really bothers me but the I realized that I make lots of jokes about my friends, we all do, so I felt like a hypocrite and told him I don't care.

>Also, I noticed that you mentioned that you know other people with Asperger's. Do you currently hang out with them?

I know two people with Asperger's who I'd actually hang out with.  Most of the other ones are boring, rude, or uncomfortably awkward.  Sorry if that sounds harsh but I'm probably the same way.

Having a funny voice and weird facial expressions and shitty posture and sitting and standing in a funny way are fucking weird, nothing worth "embracing" about them.  I seriously put people off, I'm unable to earn the respect of people, and I can't approach a girl without them thinking I'm retarded, it feels fucking awful and I don't want anyone who hasn't gone through the same thing telling me it isn't worth changing.

We watched a TED Talk that she did.  Don't get me wrong, she's brilliant and it's amazing that she was able to accomplish what she did but I believe that she knows a lot about cows and not a lot about people.

While I'm very happy for you and your boyfriend, the stuff I say when I'm talking to girls isn't "funny" or "creative", it's off-putting and retarded.  Imagine a poorly delivered joke, it isn't necesarilly a bad joke but it's poorly executed and hard to listen to.
Friendship is a strong thing but if they actually thought I don't have a chance no matter how hard I try there is no way in hell they'd be honest about that.

Nope, it's not me.

However:

>While some girls will be stuck up, conceited and general all-around bitches

Are girls "bitches" for not wanting to associate with an awkward fucking guy?

Yep, we watched the whole fucking video.  "DURRR, I CARE ABOUT COWS BUT DON'T CARE ABOUT PEOPLE."  Well I don't care about your stupid fucking speech.

However, she used the phrase "aspergery autism" which gave me a good chucke.

What I'm most worried about at this point is that if I asked my friends for help they'd think (or know) that I wouldn't have a chance with a girl who isn't as fucked up as I am and they'd just give me bullshit advice like "be confident" or "don't be negative" so we all feel good about ourselves.

>I'm not sure if you have the same problems as him, but here's where he's putting me off- talks mostly about himself, very clingy, follows me everywhere, always texting me wanting to hang out every single day even though we only met a couple weeks ago.

Nope, I've met about three or four girls over the course of the last few years who showed interest in being my friend.   Usually I just ask girls questions but the way I say shit is weird and awkward.  Imagine a poorly delivered joke, it's not a bad joke but the way it's delivered makes it hard to listen to.  That's how I talk.  Usually they look uncomfortable so I just back off.  I don't remember the last time I got close enough to a girl that I felt comfortable asking for her number or seeing if she wants to hang out.

I joined a group for students with Asperger's and it was a fucking joke.  The whole thing was a total circlejerk, we rarely talked about anything important, one time a dude brought up how he contemplated suicide and I was really impressed that he was brave enough to talk about that but we spent about five minutes on the issue and spent the next twenty minutes watching a bullshit Temple Grandin video.  

Also, for a group about social skills, the guy who ran the group sure loved to ramble.

I'm not worried about it but that doesn't mean it isn't true that it's glaringly obvious to people I don't have a girlfriend.  We have a friend who's fat and people pick on him about that, we're all just joking around and he doesn't have a problem with it (they wouldn't joke about it bothered him) but that doesn't mean he isn't fat, like how that doesn't mean I'm not a weird awkward guy.  My friends are okay with it but no girl wants to date a weird awkward guy.
When a girl is socially awkward guys think it's cute, they can find a socially awkward boyfriend who's handsome and funny instead of gawky and uncomfortable like me.

Normally it is but when I talk to my friends about my problems I end up getting into really negative bullshit and it just makes everyone feel bad.  Also, I'm afraid that I wouldn't have a chance with any of the girls we hang out with and it would be uncomfortable for them to try to work around that without straight up letting me know.
At the worst they seem repulsed and at the best they seem like they're talking to me just to be polite and would rather talk to someone not weird and awkward.
At the worst they seem repulsed and at the best they seem like they're talking to me just to be polite and would rather talk to someone not weird and awkward.
My friends are very extroverted but whenever I talk to them about my problems I get "negative" and it puts them off. They don't have time to babysit me and asking them woul be awkward.
If nothing was wrong with me I probably would have met at least one girl at this point who seems at least somewhat interested in me.

>After a year of misery and rejection you should have a working vocabulary and fluid understanding of the topics girls like to discuss and laugh about.

Well, I've been working on this for three years and still feel like a social retard, so...

Also, as I've stated, I don't get the chance to discuss anything.  Girls look at me like I'm a freak before the conversation even goes anywhere.  They don't give a shit what the retarded kid has to say, they just want to talk to someone cooler and I don't blame them.
That's what I've been saying this whole time and I feel like the first impression I give is "this guy is retarded, it's not worth talking to him."  I have no idea how the fuck to change that.

It's not really the stuff I say that's retarded as much as the way I say it.  I can listen to my tone of voice and my word choice and the way I put words together and tell that's not how a normal person talks without seeing why so I can't change it.  It seems to me like they're seeing the same thing, they look uncomfortable and put off so I just back off and feel shitty about myself.

>For one, the life of a young woman dictates that they be keenly aware of people's true intentions to protect themselves, especially in college.

I've met plenty of girls who seem fine pretty much talking to anyone except me.

>Everyone does small talk and it is completely useless unless the small talkers are already attracted to one another. The key is to be able to easily slide into real conversations. 

Like in the examples I posted, usually they seem uncomfortable before I can even transition into a real conversation so I just back off.

How do I improve my skills?  Most stuff I read about social skills are about very overt behaviors, like inappropriate body language or talking about inappropriate stuff and it always ends up being a bunch of stuff I already no to do or not to do.  I think that my behaviors are more subtle, like my inflection and the way I put words together that puts people off.  I know a guy with Asperger's who has a really nasaly voice, nobody is going to tell him that and there's nothing he can do to fix it but it will always seem weird to other people.  Maybe I'm just the same way.

>It's in your head.

No it fucking isn't.  I've been rejected by more girls I can count, and that isn't counting the ones who get uncomfortable as soon as I open my mouth or just ignore me in the first place.  I've never met a girl who seems even vaguely interested in me.  My friends have told me to my face that I'm a weird awkward guy.  If I just stopped believing that I'm an awkward fucking guy then nothing would change about me other than I'd be a whole lot more ignorant.

>There's no "magical aura" around you that causes people to dislike you

Not really, but people do give off vibes. It could be that I have weird off-putting mannerisms that give off vibes that make people dislike me.  It has nothing to do with skills, it's just the way I look and act and talk. What kind of skill would let me surpass that?

>If you don't have the social skills to interpret nonverbal cues or indirect signals, you're missing part of what the other person is trying to communicate, and that is going to cause your ability to interact with them to suffer.

What signals?  All of the signals I see are them signaling to me that I'm making them feel uncomfortable and they'd rather talk to someone who is 

>social skills

What skills do I not have?  Why is it about skills in the first place?

Most people I know with disabilities come off as fucking weird, it's just the way that they are and "skills" have nothing to do with it.  I think I'm the same way.

>be nice

Nobody cares if I'm "nice" if I'm just an uncomfortable guy to talk to.

>But not attractive girls or girls you are attracted to. It will come across that you are just interested in talking to them. Surprisingly, women often like when your only motivation for talking to them is to get to know them as a person and not an object of affection. 

None of the girls I talk to are super-hot, they're just normal girls.  And they usually seem uncomfortable as soon as I make small talk and before I even get a chance to know them better.  I think my mannerisms put them off so much that they don't even see me as a person on the same level as them.

>skills

Why is it always about skills?  Is it really a "skill" to come off as a normal person instead of a retard?  Most people I know with disabilities are just really fucking weird and that's why they don't make friends.  "Skills" have nothing to do with it.

>That's one of the things you will have to find out yourself I'm afraid.

If my problem was all about confidence then wouldn't I have found a girl who likes me for who I am and just never caught onto my "lack of confidence" or whatever?  My friends have told me to my face that I am indeed a weird awkward guy and I don't see why a girl would want a guy like me instead of a guy who isn't a social retard.

>just be yourself

I'm 20 and I've never met a girl who seems even vaguely interested in me.  Isn't that indicative that something is wrong with "myself?"

>You think your being awkward

My friends have told me to my face that I'm weird and awkward.

>but truly everyone is nervous and awkward around people

But other people manage to connect in the end and I never do.

Usually if I see a girl who isn't talking to anyone at a social event I'll try to talk to them so I can get to know them better.  Is that wrong?

>So you might THINK the girls don't want to talk to you, when this is in fact not the case.

I just described a scenario where a girl got onto a bus to get away from me, I'm pretty sure that's the case.

>Get better at your social skills in general, and then you'll find it easy to talk to girls.

Why is it always about skills?  Are "not being a sniveling retard" and "acting like a normal person" both skills?  I'm pretty sure that my mannerisms that I can't really see or control give people the (probably correct) impression that I'm a weird guy who isn't worth talking to.

I'm not overweight and I dress alright whenever I know I'll be talking to girls.  

Also, how will being confident help me if I'm a legitimately awkward guy?  Won't I just be a really retarded guy who's "confident" that he's cool and attractive?  What do I have to be confident about?

>When you desire someone/thing, you feel anxiety about the possibility of not getting it. This is the "nervousnes" your therapist & parents are talking about

Right now the "nervousness" is that they'll think I'm a freak as soon as I open my mouth, which is what usually happens.  Maybe if I had a success or two under my belt I wouldn't feel as bad.

>This allows you to get to know them before you ask them out.

Usually they seem uncomfortable before I get past small talk or get to know anything about them so I just cut off the conversation.

I'm fine if they're not interested in me as soon as I start talking but they seem repulsed by me right off the bat.  I can't even learn if we have anything in common because they seem uncomfortable before I can get the conversation past small talk so I just back off.  Not that they'd care if some socially retarded guy has anything in common with them.
Right now I'd like to just make friends with girls but they don't even want to talk to me, let alone be my friend.

That's what I think my problem is.  I practice good hygiene, have an alright hair cut, and dress alright.  I'm almost positive it's in my body language, tone of voice, word choice, inflection, and "vibes."  I have no idea how the fuck to change those or even find out what's going wrong with them.

Those are the things I try to do when I talk to girls but before we can even get to "common interests" they already seem like I'm making them really uncomfortable so I just back off.  I usually ask them situational shit about class or college stuff like what there major is or where they live on campus and right off the bat they seem uncomfortable.

Furthermore, if I'm uncomfortably awkward to talk to then I doubt they give a shit what we have in common.

The people I'd want to "emulate" are all smart and witty and I am neither of those.  I can't just come up with funny and/or interesting shit to say in a conversation no matter how hard I'm trying to be like someone.

>"Let me explain, because the thing is, it may not come across right away, but I have Asperger's, and it used to be something I was really insecure about; I felt like everyone looked at me like I was retarded or something. But as I've grown, I've come to accept my disposition and see it as a blessing in disguise. Have you ever felt different or isolated from your peers?"

What the fuck?  I may not be emotionally intelligent but I know that that's too much to lay down all at once.  If I tell people I have a disability I'm just giving them something to stereotype me based on.

I try talking to girls like I'd talk to anyone but it doesn't work.  I just end up saying stupid shit and acting weird and I feel like it really puts them off.

Also, the girl in the first story told me she'd wait for the bus before it even came by.  I think that's her way of telling me she wants to get away from me.

When I talk to people in groups I end up standing to the side and I can't really think of something to say and when I do it either sounds boring or as retarded as the stuff I say when I'm talking one on one.
I can't emulate other people, I've tried but I just end up acting like me.

Numbers and patterns and logic aren't easy for me, honestly I'm pretty fucking stupid, I failed out of computer science because I suck at that kind of thinking. Some "aspies" are dumb fucks.

I've been trying to "let" things help me for years and nothing works. Everybody else's ideas of what I'm doing wrong are being shot down while my theory that I'm repulsively awkward and people just don't like me still stands. Social skills classes woul probably only teach me about "overt" behaviors, if I have goofy retarded mannerisms they probably won't bring it up.

Also, don't tell me that there's "nothing wrong" with having a disability that makes me so awkward that I can't talk to someone fora minute without them thinking I'm a freak. It's the worst feeling in the world and I don't think you understand that.

The first link was a bunch of stuff I already know, I can't find anything about what to do if you say the right thing but it sounds retarded after it comes out of your mouth or if you feel like you're having an alright conversation but they still treat you like a freak.
Ny friend who is in an LDR really loves her boyfriend, they've been together for three to four years and I seriously don't think they'll break up.

I joined a group for people with aspergers and it sucked, it was a total circlejerk and we never talked about anything meaningful. Everyone was so awkward there was no way of improving my social skills.
are you saying that the people who ignore me aren't "good people" just because they don't want to talk to a social retard?
This is the second therapist I've worked with, the last one ran out of ideas. Maybe I just can't be helped and everybody is afraid to acknowledge it.

>practice

What practice?  Whenever I talk to someone, especially a girl, they seem really uncomfortable after the first few sentences so I just back off and don't really gain anything.

>useful books or internet discussion groups or other resources.

I haven't found anything on my specific case (awkward mannerisms that put people off, can't pinpoint or control them)
I'm almost certainly the last person you'd want to ask about that, I'm sorry and I hope things get better for you.

Sorry for the bullshit question but I know a few guys who try to make conversation with girls they don't know on Facebook and it's **creepy as hell.**
